payload.because: Sofar's record is already agent-agnostic (JSONL + MCP + CLI), so only the trigger and the spawn are Claude-Code-shaped; designing those against the record instead of against hooks is what makes the driver portable, resumable and auditable — two driver implementations can pick up the same run. Usage reporting is the least portable thing across vendors, so the model-agnostic policy must not depend on it. Building the agent loop is building Cursor: for a model without an agent, adapt an existing multi-model headless loop (OpenCode) instead.
payload.chose: Architecture: the driver is a stateless fold over the record. The record is the queue — next task comes from the plan fold, and every launch, handoff (reason: threshold | task_done | stall | needs_user) and stop is an event whose schema lives in packages/schema. Agents are reached through a three-call adapter — launch(digest, task), usage() → tokens, wait() → {exit, wrote_back} — Claude Code first, a second headless agent to prove the contract. Policy is task-scoped by default (one task per session, no context sensor needed, identical on every model); a context threshold is an optional optimisation that packs small tasks into one session. Tasks may carry model/effort hints and the driver routes per task.
payload.over: An in-session orchestrator spawning subagents per task (the orchestrator's context still grows with results, subagents cannot be resumed, and worker write-backs muddle one-session-one-record); a driver that keeps its own run state; a threshold-only policy that depends on vendor usage reporting; or implementing an agent loop inside sofar for models that lack one.
payload.rule: The driver holds no state outside the record and never implements an agent loop of its own — it launches existing headless agents through the adapter, and every driver-side state change is an event in packages/schema.

"""Exact single-occurrence replace. stdin: OLD block, a line '=====', NEW block."""
import sys

src = open(path, encoding='utf8').read()

payload.text: Phase 3 second-adapter candidate: fx (vercel-labs/fx, https://fx.sh/docs). Native coding agent written in Zig, Apache-2.0, 6.3 MiB single binary, ~10us cold start, model- and provider-agnostic, installed via a setup.sh script into ~/.local/bin. It is maximally unlike the Claude Code adapter (native binary, not a Node process; different flag surface), which is exactly what makes it good proof that the three-call contract is not shaped around adapter one. Non-interactive entry point is `fx ask` with a json output flag: docs say `output` carries accumulated assistant Markdown across the request and `final_output` only the completed final assistant response — that is the wait() payload. TWO GAPS to verify before committing it: (1) the docs do not mention token-usage reporting, and usage() is one of the three calls — if fx cannot report tokens, either the contract makes usage() optional or the context-threshold handoff reason is unavailable for this adapter and only task_done/stall/needs_user apply; (2) exit-code behaviour is undocumented. fx is also an MCP CLIENT (stdio + streamable HTTP), so it can consume the sofar MCP server directly — the driver would not need a separate context-injection path for it. Found while answering a runtime question, not while doing 1.3.

payload.because: An adapter asserting write-back would be claiming record state it never checked, the exact shape of the conflict line that asserted liveness it never tested (3c909f0); the record is the truth and the driver already folds it. The fx note (2026-08-29) records that the leading second adapter may not report tokens, and the contract must not be shaped around adapter one. A wrong session guess files a handoff on someone else's session, which corrupts the run's history silently, while a stall is loud and recoverable.
payload.chose: Adapter contract details (1.3): an adapter is a process wrapper and nothing more. launch(request) returns a handle with usage(), optional nudge(), kill() and wait(); capabilities {usage, nudge, model, effort} are declared up front and the threshold policy is REFUSED on an adapter lacking usage or nudge (policyUnavailable), so usage() is optional in effect — fx reports no tokens and still runs the task policy identically. wrote_back is DERIVED from the fold (wroteBack: the session is registered and carries a summary), never reported by the adapter. Session identity: the adapter passes on a session id only when its transport showed one; otherwise the driver diffs sessions registered by that tool since the launch, takes a single candidate, and treats several as ambiguous, never a guess (resolveLaunchedSession).

payload.because: A prose matcher would assert a state it never tested — the shape D3 already rejected for wrote_back and 3c909f0 for liveness — and it would silently mis-stop on wording the driver's author never imagined. `blocked` is the record's existing word for "wants to happen, cannot yet", carries a mandatory reason, and is visible to every surface without new schema. Requiring the write-back for task_done keeps the two halves of a handoff honest: the queue only truly advanced when the record says both that the task closed and what the next session should do.
payload.chose: Handoff reasons are read STRUCTURALLY from the fold, never from write-back prose (2.2). needs_user = the task the driver named is `blocked` after the session — a status that already requires a note, so the operator's question is recorded where the next reader looks. task_done = the session wrote back AND some task reached a terminal status (done or dropped). Everything else is a stall, including a session that finished work but skipped its write-back: the next session resumes from the next_action, so an unwritten session leaves the queue exactly where it was. The prompt states the blocked lever verbatim, so the agent triggers the stop deliberately instead of the driver inferring it.
payload.over: Matching next_action prose for "ask the user"/"operator"/"decide"; a new needs_user event; treating any task status change (pending→active) as progress; trusting the adapter's exit code as the verdict.
payload.rule: Driver handoff reasons are derived from the fold — needs_user is the named task in status `blocked`, task_done needs a write-back AND a terminal task status; never infer a reason from write-back prose or an exit code.

payload.because: Sessions in a run are SEQUENTIAL and cumulative — session N+1 continues session N's work — so a fresh checkout per session discards uncommitted work and re-pays every setup cost the tree carries (node_modules above all: a worktree with no install cannot run `npm test`, and the acceptance criteria are tests). Isolation between sessions is not a thing a sequential run needs; isolation from the OPERATOR's tree is, and an operator who wants it can point `--cwd` at a worktree they set up once. The verification is the part that actually matters: the record is committed, so a plain worktree carries a STALE COPY of it, and a session writing there would fork the queue invisibly — realpath equality is the cheap check that catches exactly that.
payload.chose: One working directory per RUN, not one worktree per session (2.2, superseding the plan text of 2.2). `sofar drive` launches every session with cwd = the repo root by default, or `--cwd <dir>` for a worktree the OPERATOR made; the driver creates no worktree and switches no branch. Before the first launch it verifies that `<cwd>/.sofar/initiatives/<slug>/events.jsonl` resolves (realpath) to the log it is driving, and refuses otherwise; it also warns when the launch directory's branch binds to a different initiative, since that is the digest the child's SessionStart hook will inject.
payload.over: A fresh `git worktree add` per session, as 2.2's plan text says; the driver creating and removing worktrees itself; symlinking `.sofar` into a worktree on the session's behalf.
payload.rule: `sofar drive` never creates or destroys a git worktree or switches a branch; it launches into one directory for the whole run and refuses to start unless that directory's `.sofar` log for the initiative is the same file it is driving.
